info.description: HTTP API of CandleStack, a lab for experiments on financial time series. Market data covers crypto from Binance and US stocks from Alpaca. Times in responses are UTC epoch seconds; requests also accept ISO 8601. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`). [Website](https://candlestack.tech) · [Source code](https://github.com/candlestack-tech/candlestack) · [Status](https://ops.candlestack.tech)
info.title: CandleStack API

get.description:
200 when the app, its Redis and its Postgres work, 503 with the same body when one of
them does not.

The body is compact JSON: deploy checks look for `"version":"<version>"` and the commit.

Reachability of Binance (`GET /api/v3/ping`) and Alpaca (`GET /v2/clock`), checked at
most once a minute. 200 when both answer, 503 with the same body when one does not.

The account the beta list just turned away, for the sign-in page; 404 when this browser
was not turned away in the last 10 minutes.

get.description:
Redirects to the provider's sign-in page, or to `/signin?error=failed` when sign-in
with it is not available or this address made too many sign-in requests in a minute. A
provider's account that never signed in joins the CandleStack user with its email, so the
email links a user's GitHub and Google; it signs in to a new user when no user has it.

With `intent=connect` (signed in, a link of Settings) the provider's account is added to
the signed-in user's sign-in methods instead: the callback returns to `next` (default
`/settings/sign-in`), or to `/settings/sign-in?error=taken` when that account already
signs in to another CandleStack user, or `/settings/sign-in?error=failed`, also right away
when the request does not come from the app's own pages.

post.description:
Starts a backtest of one of the user's models on one instrument and period and returns
its document, `running`, with its number. Checked first: the model is the user's and has a
manifest, the instrument fits the model, the period with the candles the model needs before
it fits the data and the candle limit, the user has no other backtest running, and the
worker that runs the models can be reached. The run goes on after the response; the
document (`GET /api/v1/backtests/{backtest_id}`) has the results once it finished.

403.description: The request does not come from the app's own pages (`cross-origin-request`).

404.description: The user has no model with this ID (`not-found`), or the instrument is not in the catalog (`instrument-not-found`).

409.description: The model has no manifest (`model-needs-setup`), or another backtest of the user is running (`backtest-running`).

422.description: An invalid setup (`validation`), a model of another market (`instrument-not-for-model`), a period outside the data (`period-out-of-range`), without the candles the model needs before it (`warm-up-out-of-range`), or with more candles than allowed (`too-many-candles`).

502.description: A data source sent candles that failed validation (`source-data-invalid`).

503.description: A data source cannot be reached (`source-unavailable`), or for a new backtest the worker that runs the models (`backtests-unavailable`).

get.description:
The result document of the backtest, whatever its status (`results` is null until it
finished), in the light view: a series of more than 10,000 rows has one point per UTC day,
and only the newest 10,000 trades are in it (`trades.complete` false).

404.description: The user has no backtest with this ID (`not-found`).

409.description: The backtest is test data that has no result document (`no-document`).

502.description: A data source sent candles that failed validation (`source-data-invalid`).

503.description: A data source cannot be reached (`source-unavailable`), or for a new backtest the worker that runs the models (`backtests-unavailable`).

the best finished ones by Sharpe ratio, return, drawdown and win rate, and the best
starred ones.

Searches the instruments of both markets: every Binance spot pair that is trading and
every active tradable US stock and ETF at Alpaca (without OTC). Each item carries its last
price, 24 h change and 24 h volume in USD, refreshed every few minutes, its last 10 daily
candles (`spark`), refreshed once a day (null without them), and the open time of its first
candle (`available_from`, null while not known yet).

Ranking: the top pair of a crypto base asset equal to the query (`btc` finds `BTCUSDT`
first), exact symbol, the other pairs of that base asset, symbol prefix, prefix of a word
in the name, substring of the symbol, substring of the name; ties go to `sort`, then to the
shorter symbol, then alphabetically. Without `q`, every instrument comes back in `sort`:
the most traded first by default.
`exchange` narrows any of these to the instruments that trade on it.
`total` counts all matches: page through them with `offset` and `limit`.

When the instrument list of one market cannot be loaded, the other market is still
searched and `unavailable` names the missing one; 503 when no market can be searched.

post.description:
Uploads a model file, Keras (`.keras`) or ONNX (`.onnx`): the body is the file, `name`
its file name. The file is checked before it is kept: `opens` (a real model of its format
with no custom code inside, for ONNX the standard operators only, all in the one file, with
one float32 input and output; nothing from the file is executed) and `weights` (it holds
trained weights). A file with a name the user already has gets a number, as
`lstm (2).keras`. The model is `needs_setup` until its manifest is added
(`PUT /api/v1/models/{model_id}/manifest`).

put.description:
Adds the model's manifest, or replaces the one it has; the body is the manifest. It is
kept only when every check passes: its form, the catalog (every block exists, in its
step), the blocks' parameters, the names of the columns, the signature against the window
and the columns, the shapes of the example, and the signature against the input and
output the upload read from the model file. The model is then `ready`. A trial run in the
worker follows after the answer: the model becomes `verified` when it gives the output of
the manifest's example, and a failed run leaves it `ready` with its `check_error`.

403.description: The request does not come from the app's own pages (`cross-origin-request`).

404.description: The user has no model with this ID (`not-found`).

413.description: The manifest is larger than 1 MB (`manifest-too-large`).

422.description: A check failed (`manifest-check-failed`): `problems` lists what is wrong, at most 10, each with its `check` (`schema`, `catalog`, `params`, `names`, `signature`, `example` or `model`) and a `detail` of one sentence; `more_problems` counts the rest and `unknown_blocks` names the blocks the catalog does not have. `detail` says the same in words.

get.description:
Every block a model's manifest can name, by step (representation, feature,
normalization, window): its versioned id, what it does, its warm-up and its parameters
with their types, ranges and defaults. The app builds the manifest form from it. A block
that is not listed yet makes a manifest that cannot run.
